lead: Selpercatinib sensitivity resembles EXT1, EXT2, SLC35B2, HS2ST1 and FGFR2 knockout
precedent: Kooijman et al. measured WT FGFR2 enzyme inhibition (IC50 16 nM) and about tenfold greater cellular potency in an FGFR1–3-altered group. FDA study LOXO-292-PHARM-010 measured inhibition of stimulated WT FGFR2 phosphorylation in inducible HEK293 cells (IC50 242 nM). A heparin–FGF1–FGFR2 structure and a separate FGFR1 co-dependency network containing all four HS genes support pathway biology. The selpercatinib-specific four-gene knockout signature was not located.
citations: Kooijman et al. 2022, Table 2 and Fig 3D, https://doi.org/10.3389/fonc.2022.953013 | FDA NDA 213246 (2020), LOXO-292-PHARM-010, no DOI, https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213246Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf | Pellegrini et al. 2000, FGF1–FGFR2–heparin structural complex, https://doi.org/10.1038/35039551 | Functional genomic analysis of adult and pediatric brain tumor isolates (bioRxiv), Fig 4, https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.01.05.522885 | Barnett et al. 2002, GDNF/RET HS dependence, https://doi.org/10.1242/jcs.00114 | Wang et al. 2021, selpercatinib transport, https://doi.org/10.3390/ph14111087
confounds: FGFR and ligand-dependent RET signaling both use HS. The four genes could mark a shared growth-factor-dependent cell state. Lineage or FGFR/RET driver status can structure sensitivities within tissue classes. ABCB1-mediated selpercatinib efflux is experimentally established, but its contribution to this association is unmeasured.
limitations: No direct HS-enzyme inhibition established. #96 Sanger/RNAi replication refers to EXT1 only; EXT1 missed RNAi replication. Published cell-group contrasts are not an independent measurement of the four-gene signature. Negative search is bounded by source coverage.

lead: Zanubrutinib sensitivity resembles ERBB2 and EGFR knockout
precedent: Kooijman et al. reported preferential growth inhibition of ERBB2-amplified (45-fold) and EGFR-mutant (8-fold) cell lines and biochemical EGFR activity. Dostálová et al. directly tested zanubrutinib in HER2-positive breast cancer cells, documenting pathway phosphorylation loss and growth inhibition. NCI-60 profiling linked its response pattern to EGFR inhibitors. The biological selectivity is published; the identical PRISM-to-knockout correlation was not located.
citations: Kooijman et al. 2022, Table 2 and Figs 2E/8B, https://doi.org/10.3389/fonc.2022.953013 | Dostálová et al. 2023, HER2-positive cells and ERBB signaling, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10637-023-01346-7 | Morris et al. 2023, NCI-60 sensitivity fingerprints, https://doi.org/10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-23-0267 | Guo et al. 2019, BTK inhibitor selectivity, https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jmedchem.9b00687 | FDA NDA 213217 (2019), study R01-BIOL-148, Table 3, no DOI, https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/213217Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
confounds: HER2 amplification, EGFR activation, epithelial lineage and ERBB pathway co-dependence may structure the profile. Prior biochemical and driver-selected cell data favor ERBB-pathway pharmacology. An across-line fitness assay cannot apportion lethality between receptors or rule out cytostasis.
limitations: Drug inhibition was assayed in molecularly selected lines. Mutation or amplification is a proxy for dependency. #96 replicated its top gene ERBB2 in both genetic resources; those rows do not assess EGFR replication.

lead: PBT-1033 (PBT2) sensitivity tracks HSCB, LYRM4 and IREB2 knockout across cancer cell lines.
precedent: The PBT-1033 and PBT2 preparations share the same 5,7-dichloro-2-[(dimethylamino)methyl]quinolin-8-ol parent structure; the cited preparations use its hydrochloride. PBT2 perturbs metal handling. Proteomics after PBT2 exposure in H. pylori showed reduced abundance of Fe–S assembly and respiratory proteins. Tumor-cell imaging showed altered copper distribution and copper-dependent cytotoxicity. No retrieved report tested the named human knockout–sensitivity profile. HSCB and LYRM4 support Fe–S biogenesis; IREB2 regulates cellular iron availability.
citations: Chen et al., mBio (2026), Fig. 2, bacterial proteomics, PMID 42294673, https://doi.org/10.1128/mbio.01229-26 | Summers et al., Metallomics (2020), tumor-cell metal imaging, PMID 33169753, https://doi.org/10.1039/D0MT00222D | Human ISD11 and iron homeostasis, Hum Mol Genet (2009), PMID 19454487, https://doi.org/10.1093/hmg/ddp239 | IUPHAR/BPS PBT2 ligand 11108 (identity), https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/GRAC/LigandDisplayForward?ligandId=11108 | Barnham et al., US20060089380A1, Example 15 (PBT 1033 structure), no DOI, https://patents.google.com/patent/US20060089380A1/en | Bohlmann et al., mBio (2018), compound 3 (PBT2 HCl structure), https://doi.org/10.1128/mBio.02391-18
confounds: Assay context: extracellular metal availability changes PBT2 toxicity. Metal-homeostasis or respiratory state could explain susceptibility without direct inhibition of an assembly factor. The PRISM medium explanation was not tested.
limitations: The broad Europe PMC named-gene query returned 29 titles, mostly iron biology or neurodegeneration reviews; adding the drug-screen terms returned zero. Bacterial proteomics and metal imaging do not establish a human cancer target. #96 replication statistics apply to HSCB alone. Unindexed supplements can escape this search.

lead: Ruboxistaurin (LY333531) sensitivity tracks PPM1D and MDM2 knockout, suggesting a TP53-wild-type response state.
precedent: Vermeulen et al. Table S6 tested ruboxistaurin in overlapping PRISM 23Q4 records against TP53 mutation status. The damaging-variant comparison favored greater sensitivity in the reference group (r=0.1413, ANOVA p=0.00340, FDR=0.342). The hotspot comparison also missed correction (r=0.0832, FDR=0.980). A dissertation reported reduced p53 T329 phosphorylation after ruboxistaurin during genotoxic stress. No located prior tested this drug's PPM1D/MDM2 knockout profile. Miller et al. linked the two dependencies to functional p53. Ruboxistaurin also has direct PIM1 pharmacology.

confounds: TP53 functional status is the leading shared-state explanation. Lineage and FLT3/PIM1 or PKC pharmacology are additional alternatives. The source model used lineage and expression PCs but did not directly condition on TP53 function. RNAi replicated the top PPM1D match, while Sanger missed its FDR cutoff. limitations: The earlier REP.1M condition (BRD-K27677357-003-04-9 at 2.5 µM) overlaps #96. Neither prior mutation comparison passed FDR correction. The reference category can carry TP53 variants outside the class tested. The phosphorylation observation is distinct from a selective-viability endpoint. ChEMBL coverage is limited to the specified curated human single-protein targets and parent molecule.

lead: NIM811 sensitivity tracks SLC33A1 knockout across cancer cell lines.
precedent: A 2024 patent publication and the investigators’ public grant report describe NIM811 and SLC33A1 loss each sensitizing EGFR-mutant lung cancer models to osimertinib. This establishes priority for a conditional phenocopy. The retrieved reports do not show a pan-cancer, single-agent sensitivity correlation or direct NIM811 binding to SLC33A1.
citations: Meyerson & Golomb, WO2024220666A2 (published 2024-10-24), Figs. 1–2, 7, 9, patent application, no DOI, https://patents.google.com/patent/WO2024220666A2/en | Golomb, LCRF-AstraZeneca Research Grant final report (grant awarded 2021; posting date unstated), no DOI, https://www.lungcancerresearchfoundation.org/research/our-investigators/previously-funded-research/2021-lcrf-astrazeneca-research-grant-dana-farber-cancer-institute-lior-golomb-phd/ | Romero et al., Nat Cancer (2020), KEAP1/NRF2 context, PMID 34414377, https://doi.org/10.1038/s43018-020-0071-1 | Liu et al., Nat Cell Biol (2026), ER oxidized glutathione transport, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41556-026-01922-y | Wang et al., Cell Death Dis (2017), NIM811 and ER stress in glioblastoma cells, PMID 28518150, https://doi.org/10.1038/cddis.2017.217
confounds: Lineage, KEAP1/NRF2 genotype and ER redox state could jointly select sensitive models. SLC33A1 loss selectively compromises KEAP1-mutant lung models; a lineage indicator does not remove within-lineage genotype effects. No attribution of the PRISM correlation to those variables was tested. NIM811 also induced ER-stress-associated cell death in glioblastoma cells, a plausible route to convergent sensitivity.
limitations: For the named pair, PubMed and Europe PMC each returned zero; the broader family-name Europe PMC query returned 27 titles. No peer-reviewed report of the specific NIM811 phenocopy was identified. The patent and grant report are from the same group and compare sensitization to osimertinib. Unindexed supplements can escape this search.

lead: Eribulin, DM4 (ravtansine), soblidotin, mivobulin, batabulin and crolibulin sensitivity tracks DARS1 knockout.
precedent: Sultan et al. identified DARS1 as a paclitaxel sensitivity gene in a pooled MDA-MB-231 xenograft shRNA screen. Cells carrying sensitivity-gene hairpins gained relative fitness under paclitaxel. DARS1 expression was lower in a paclitaxel-resistant derivative. This is a drug-by-knockdown interaction with a different microtubule agent. The study validated BCL6 individually. No located paper reported the six named agents’ untreated DARS1 dependency versus drug-sensitivity correlation.
citations: Sultan et al. (2021), paclitaxel shRNA screen and expression comparison, https://doi.org/10.1002/1878-0261.12964 (Results 3.1–3.2, Fig. S6). Smith et al. (2010), eribulin binds tubulin and microtubule ends, https://doi.org/10.1021/bi901810u. Hafner et al. (2016), division-rate effects on viability metrics, https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.3853. (2015), eribulin sensitivity and doubling time in eight breast lines, PMID 26504006, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26504006/. Corsello et al. (2020), PRISM repurposing viability profiling, https://doi.org/10.1038/s43018-019-0018-6.
confounds: Proliferation/mitotic rate and fixed-time viability can yield shared sensitivity. Nearly every line crossed the source activity threshold for these six drugs, which limits specificity. ABCB1/efflux is documented for eribulin and should not be assigned to all six without measurements. In eight breast lines eribulin GI50 did not correlate with doubling time, so proliferation alone is unproved. #96 Sanger replication met FDR for eribulin, batabulin and crolibulin only; DARS1 RNAi was unavailable in its table.
limitations: Paclitaxel is outside the six compounds and has different effects on microtubules. Neither the shRNA interaction nor expression in a resistant derivative is a baseline cross-line DARS1 dependency analysis. DARS/DARs also retrieves antibody drug-to-antibody ratio. A shared cytotoxic profile has no direct target specificity. Free DM4 was unmapped in ChEMBL by preferred name and PubChem structure key. The DARS1 activity query covered the other five parent molecules only.
